subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Suppose that an urn B₁ contains 2 white and 3 black balls and another urn B₂ contains 3 white and 4 black balls. One urn is selected at random and a ball is drawn from it. If the ball drawn is found black, find the probability that the urn chosen was B₁.

mark_split.label: Prior probabilities of choosing each container
Probability of the colour from each container

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that the black ball came from B₁ — the events, the priors, the two black-ball probabilities, the total, and Bayes.
insider_note: The urn is chosen first and the colour is seen second; the question asks the REVERSE direction, which is exactly what Bayes is for. The denominator 41/70 is where arithmetic slips happen.

steps.label: Define the events
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two events for the two urns, one event for the colour seen. Name all three before writing any number.
steps.memory_tip: Do not reuse the letter B for both the urn and the black-ball event. Name all three.

lines.text: Let E₁, E₂ be the events of selecting urn B₁
and urn B₂ respectively, and let B be the
event that the ball drawn is black.

recall.must_convey: That E₁ and E₂ are the events of choosing urn B₁ and B₂, and B is the event that the drawn ball is black.

E one is urn one chosen E two is urn two chosen B is black ball

name the two urn events and the black ball event

steps.why: Bayes' theorem is written in terms of named events. The urn events are the mutually exclusive and exhaustive ones; the colour event is the A of the theorem.
common_mistakes: Using the same letter B for the urn B₁ and for the black-ball event.
Not writing the colour event at all and then having no symbol for the condition.

steps.label: Priors
steps.margin_note: Second mark. "Selected at random" between two urns means each urn has probability 1/2.
steps.memory_tip: The URN is chosen at random, not a ball, so each urn is 1/2 — not 5/12 and 7/12.

lines.text: The urn is chosen at random, so

recall.must_convey: That each urn is equally likely to be chosen, so P(E₁) = P(E₂) = 1/2.
accept: each urn is chosen with probability half
P of E one equals P of E two equals one by two
the urn is picked at random so both priors are half
rendu urns ki probability half half
the prior for each urn is one half

steps.why: The priors are the probabilities BEFORE the colour is seen. They come from how the urn was chosen, not from the balls.
common_mistakes: Taking P(E₁) = 5/12 and P(E₂) = 7/12 from the number of balls — the urn, not a ball, is chosen at random.
Leaving the priors out because they are equal; they still appear in the formula.

steps.label: P(black | each urn)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Read each urn separately: B₁ has 3 black out of 5, B₂ has 4 black out of 7.
steps.memory_tip: Read each urn separately: 3 black of 5, and 4 black of 7.

recall.must_convey: That P(B|E₁) = 3/5 and P(B|E₂) = 4/7, each read from its own urn.
accept: black given urn one is three by five and black given urn two is four by seven
P of B given E one is 3 by 5 and P of B given E two is 4 by 7
from B one three black out of five, from B two four black out of seven
B one lo black probability 3 by 5, B two lo 4 by 7
the likelihoods are three fifths and four sevenths

steps.why: These are the probabilities the experiment gives directly — the colour given the urn. Bayes reverses them into the urn given the colour.
common_mistakes: Using 3/12 and 4/12 (black balls over ALL balls) instead of over each urn's own total.
Swapping the two fractions between the urns.

steps.label: Total probability of black
steps.margin_note: Two marks. P(B) = P(E₁)·P(B|E₁) + P(E₂)·P(B|E₂). Keep the fractions exact: 3/10 + 2/7 = (21 + 20)/70 = 41/70.
steps.memory_tip: Keep the fractions exact: 3/10 + 2/7 over 70 is (21 + 20)/70 = 41/70.

accept: P of B is half times three by five plus half times four by seven which is forty one by seventy
total probability of black is 3 by 10 plus 2 by 7 equals 41 by 70
add prior times likelihood for both urns to get forty one by seventy
P of black ante half into 3 by 5 plus half into 4 by 7, 41 by 70 vasthundi
the denominator of bayes is 41 by 70

steps.why: A black ball can come from either urn; the two routes are disjoint, so their probabilities add. This sum is the denominator of Bayes' theorem.
common_mistakes: Getting 3/10 + 2/7 wrong: the common denominator is 70, giving 21 + 20 = 41.
Writing 2/7 as 4/14 and then not simplifying consistently.

steps.label: Bayes' theorem
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. P(E₁|B) = P(E₁)·P(B|E₁)/P(B) = (3/10)/(41/70). Divide by a fraction by multiplying by its reciprocal; 70/10 = 7 gives 21/41.
steps.memory_tip: The forward direction 3/5 is not the answer. Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal: (3/10)(70/41) = 21/41.

accept: P of E one given B is P E one times P B given E one over P B which is three by ten over forty one by seventy equals twenty one by forty one
by bayes theorem the answer is 21 by 41
divide the urn one route three by ten by the total forty one by seventy to get twenty one by forty one
bayes prakaram 3 by 10 ni 41 by 70 tho divide cheste 21 by 41
the probability the urn was B one given black is twenty one by forty one
heard_as: three by ten over forty one by seventy

steps.why: The answer is the share of the black-ball probability that came through urn B₁: the B₁ route over all routes.
common_mistakes: Writing P(B|E₁) = 3/5 as the answer — that is the forward direction, not the one asked.
Cancelling 70 and 10 wrongly and getting 3/41 or 210/41.
